policy: Add-only. Every review-queue gloss is kept unchanged; this file adds the English evidence English Wiktionary supplies: resolved form-of lemmas, close variants, translation-table equivalents, usage examples with English translations, and romanizations. Definitions are ranked (own sense corroborated by a translation table, then own sense in Wiktionary order with obsolete/archaic/rare senses last, then resolved lemma, close variant, translation equivalent). The lead candidate is a reviewer's starting point; nothing is selected or approved.

examples.english: to inhale smoke

examples.text: 그 회견에서 내려다본 지구의 모습을 묻는 말에 『마치 연기에 가려진 것처럼 내가 잔뜩 끼여있다. 피나투보화산의 폭발 때문인지 쿠웨이트의 유전 연기 때문인지는 알 수 없지만 이제까지 세번에 걸친 우주여행에서 최악의 흐린 전망이다』고 했다.
examples.english: In the news conference, when asked about the view of Earth as seen from space, [Dr. Lucid] replied, "It was enveloped in an obscuring haze of smoke. I do not know if that is because of the eruption of Mount Pinatubo or smoke from the Kuwaiti oil fields, but it is so far the worst view I had in all of my three missions."
examples.roman: Geu hoegyeon-eseo naeryeodabon jigu-ui moseub-eul munneun mar-e machi yeon'gi-e garyeojin geot-cheoreom nae-ga jantteuk kkiyeoitda. Pinatubo-hwasan-ui pokbal ttaemun-inji Kuweiteu-ui yujeon yeon'gi ttaemun-inji-neun al su eop-jiman ije-kkaji se-beon-e geolchin ujuyeohaeng-eseo choeag-ui heurin jeonmang-idago haetda.

definitions.text: thing; something; that which; what; used to designate any object, action, or phenomenon, forming noun phrases.

examples.text: 이 중에서 제일 큰 게 뭐야?
examples.english: What's the biggest one out of these?
examples.roman: i jung-eseo jeil keun ge mwoya?

examples.text: 이 곳에는 바위 같은 것이 정말 많습니다.
examples.english: Here, there are very many things that look like rocks.
examples.roman: I gos-e-neun bawi gateun geos-i jeongmal manseumnida.

definitions.text: an object belonging to an owner; forms constructions equivalent to English possessive pronouns. Colloquially pronounced 꺼 (kkeo) with initial tensing.

examples.text: 이 세상은 우리들의 것이었지만, 이제는 너희들의 것이다.
examples.english: This world was ours, but now it’s yours.
examples.roman: I sesang-eun uri-deur-ui geos-ieotjiman, ije-neun neohui-deur-ui geos-ida.

examples.english: But this pencil is my friend's.

definitions.text: Used as a light verb to allow nouns and noun-like forms to function as active verbs. The verb itself has little to no real meaning. The noun functions as a direct object of the verb, being able to take particles such as the accusative case marker -을 or the topic marker -은.
Used as a light verb to allow nouns and noun-like forms to function as adjectives. The verb itself has little to no real meaning. The noun can be separated by the topic marker -은.
After certain roots, fully suffixed to form an inseparable verb or adjective. Such roots tend to be single-character Sino-Korean morphemes.
Used with no real meaning after a verb or adjective nominalized with -기 and followed by a particle.
Used as the neutral verbal element after suffixes expressing intent.
Used as the neutral verbal element for constructions with repeated suffixes.
and all; used after -고 to emphasize a suffix expressing causation.
See -게 하다 (-ge hada, “to make; (forms the causative)”).

definitions.text: The first syllable in the standard ordering (가나다순 (ganadasun)) of hangul, the Korean alphabet; often used to mark the first item of a list or sub-list, equivalent to English A and Japanese あ.

examples.english: riverside
streamside
I sat beside it.
The flowers were in full bloom around the Buddha.

raw_glosses: (with an implied or explicit possessor) around, nearby, beside

examples.english: those of age 15 permitted to watch
divided reimbursement allowed

definitions.text: The lowest score in the five-point grading system in South Korean schools, ultimately abolished in 2012; equivalent to E or F in the Roman alphabet grading scheme.
Root of 가하다 (gahada, “to add; to exert”). Rarely used alone.

examples.english: Jongno, third street

Used with no real meaning after a verb or adjective nominalized with -기 and followed by a particle.
Used as the neutral verbal element after suffixes expressing intent.
Used as the neutral verbal element for constructions with repeated suffixes.

definitions.text: Used as a light verb to allow nouns and noun-like forms to function as active verbs. The verb itself has little to no real meaning. The noun functions as a direct object of the verb, being able to take particles such as the accusative case marker -을 or the topic marker -은.
Used as a light verb to allow nouns and noun-like forms to function as adjectives. The verb itself has little to no real meaning. The noun can be separated by the topic marker -은.
After certain roots, fully suffixed to form an inseparable verb or adjective. Such roots tend to be single-character Sino-Korean morphemes.
Used with no real meaning after a verb or adjective nominalized with -기 and followed by a particle.
Used as the neutral verbal element after suffixes expressing intent.
Used as the neutral verbal element for constructions with repeated suffixes.
and all; used after -고 to emphasize a suffix expressing causation.
See -게 하다 (-ge hada, “to make; (forms the causative)”).

Used as the neutral verbal element after suffixes expressing intent.
Used as the neutral verbal element for constructions with repeated suffixes.

examples.text: 臣聞：「國之興也，視民如傷，是其福也。其亡也，以民為土芥，是其禍也。」

examples.text: 今欲與漢闓大關，取漢女為妻，歲給遺我糱酒萬石，稷米五千斛，雜繒萬匹，它如故約，則邊不相盜矣。
examples.english: "If you desire to establish a significant relationship with Han, tak[ing? e?] Han women as wives, annually provide us with ten thousand stones of rice wine, five thousand bushels of millet, and ten thousand pieces of mixed silk— if these terms are agreed upon, then there will be no thefts along the border."
examples.roman: Jīn yù yǔ Hàn kǎi dàguān, qǔ Hàn nǚ wéi qī, suì jǐ wèi wǒ nièjiǔ wàn dàn, jì mǐ wǔ qiān hú, zá zēng wàn pǐ, tā rú gù yuē, zé biān bù xiàng dào yǐ.

examples.text: 今欲与汉闿大关，取汉女为妻，岁给遗我糱酒万石，稷米五千斛，杂缯万匹，它如故约，则边不相盗矣。

definitions.text: introduction (initial section of a book or article which introduces subject material)
before (in store for, in the future of)
before (in front of according to an ordering system)
expression of surprise: oh, my word!
to bathe in (the sunlight, moonlight, spotlight, etc.)
to be influenced or affected by

examples.text: 요즘에는 저마다 핸드폰을 이용하여 영화를 만들 수 있는데, 이것은 예전에 할 수 있었던 것이 아니다.
examples.english: These days everyone can make a movie using their mobile phone, which we used to not be able to do.
examples.roman: Yojeum-eneun jeomada haendeupon-eul iyonghayeo yeonghwa-reul mandeul su inneunde, igeos-eun yejeon-e hal su isseotdeon geos-i anida.

definitions.text: nowadays (at the present time; in the current era)

lead_candidate.text: back (to or in a previous condition or place)

definitions.text: back (to or in a previous condition or place)
back (away from the front or from an edge)
to suffer, to sustain (harm, losses, etc.)

lead_candidate.text: to see, to look at, to watch (to perceive with the eyes)

definitions.text: to see, to look at, to watch (to perceive with the eyes)
to look after (a baby, child, house, etc.)
to try, to examine (before the meal or purchase)
Used to denote that the experience of the main verb has led to a certain conclusion or realization.
to seem (only in the present declarative conjugations)
to intend to (only in the present declarative conjugations, often threat)
to be out of fear that (only in the forms 봐 (bwa), 봐서 (bwaseo))
to be given that (only in the form 보니 (boni))
among (of a person or thing: in the midst of and surrounded by (other people or things))

lead_candidate.text: Jeolla dialect form of 주워듣다 (juwodeutda, “to pick up (information) by listening”)

definitions.text: Jeolla dialect form of 주워듣다 (juwodeutda, “to pick up (information) by listening”)

lead_candidate.text: darling (often used as an affectionate term of address: person who is very dear to one)

definitions.text: darling (often used as an affectionate term of address: person who is very dear to one)

lead_candidate.text: hmm (a common interjection used when one is trying to recall something or is in deep thought)

definitions.text: hmm (a common interjection used when one is trying to recall something or is in deep thought)

examples.text: 그의 이름이 뭐더라, 에 하며 기억을 더듬었다.
examples.english: Trying to recall his name, he muttered hmm as he searched his memory.
examples.roman: Geuui ireumi mwodeora, e hamyeo gieogeul deodeumeotda.

definitions.text: uh (an interjection used as a verbal filler when beginning to speak or hesitating mid-sentence)

examples.text: 발표를 시작하기 전에 그는 에 하며 잠시 머뭇거렸다.
examples.english: Before starting his presentation, he uttered uh as he hesitated.
examples.roman: Balpyoreul sijakhagi jeone geuneun e hamyeo jamsi meomutgeoryeotda.

definitions.text: hmph (an interjection uttered privately when one feels dissatisfied or annoyed because something does not meet one’s expectations)

examples.text: 그의 무례한 말에 에 하고 한숨을 쉬었다.
examples.english: At his rude remark, he uttered hmph and sighed.
examples.roman: Geuui muryehan mare e hago hansumeul swieotda.

definitions.text: nah (an informal interjection used to gently decline or reject something without harshness)

examples.text: 그 제안을 듣고 에 하고 가볍게 거절했다.
examples.english: Upon hearing the proposal, he responded with a casual nah.
examples.roman: Geu jeaneul deutgo e hago gabyeopge geojeolhaetda.

definitions.text: tut-tut (an interjection used to mildly admonish or scold someone)

examples.text: 아이의 장난에 어른들이 에 하며 나무랐다.
examples.english: In response to the child’s mischief, the adults gently uttered tut-tut .
examples.roman: Aiui jangnane eoreundeuri e hamyeo namuratda.

definitions.text: pshaw (an interjection used to dismiss or cut off one’s own lingering thoughts)

examples.text: 복잡한 생각이 떠오르자 그는 에 하고 생각을 끊었다.
examples.english: When complicated thoughts arose, he uttered pshaw to cut them off.
examples.roman: Bokjaphan saenggagi tteooreuja geuneun e hago saenggageul kkeuneotda.

definitions.text: ah (an interjection expressed spontaneously when one feels refreshed or pleasantly uplifted)

examples.text: 산책 후에 그는 기분 좋게 에 하고 한숨 돌렸다.
examples.english: After the walk, feeling refreshed, he exhaled ah in a contented state.
examples.roman: Sanchaek hue geuneun gibun joke e hago hansum dollyeotda.

definitions.text: e (the name of the Hangul jamo ‘ㅔ‘, one of the vowel letters in the Korean alphabet)

examples.text: 한글 자모 중 에는 독특한 음가를 나타낸다.

examples.text: 怪哉！夫子有三軍之懼，而又有桑中之喜，宜將竊妻以逃者也。
examples.english: How strange! You have the anxiety of all the armies of the State on your mind, and yet you are as bright as if proceeding to an encounter among the mulberry trees. You ought to be stealing a marriage with some lady.
examples.roman: Guài zāi! Fūzǐ yǒu sānjūn zhī jù, ér yòu yǒu sāngzhōng zhī xǐ, yí jiāng qiè qī yǐ táo zhě yě.

examples.text: 怪哉！夫子有三军之惧，而又有桑中之喜，宜将窃妻以逃者也。
examples.english: How strange! You have the anxiety of all the armies of the State on your mind, and yet you are as bright as if proceeding to an encounter among the mulberry trees. You ought to be stealing a marriage with some lady.
examples.roman: Guài zāi! Fūzǐ yǒu sānjūn zhī jù, ér yòu yǒu sāngzhōng zhī xǐ, yí jiāng qiè qī yǐ táo zhě yě.

examples.text: 曾子曰：「士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠。仁以為己任，不亦重乎？死而後已，不亦遠乎？」
examples.english: The philosopher Zeng said, "The officer may not be without breadth of mind and vigorous endurance. His burden is heavy and his course is long. Perfect virtue is the burden which he considers it is his to sustain - is it not heavy? Only with death does his course stop - is it not long?"
examples.roman: Zēngzǐ yuē: “Shì bù kěyǐ bù hóng yì, rèn zhòng ér dào yuǎn. Rén yǐ wèi jǐ rèn, bù yì zhòng hū? Sǐ ér hòu yǐ, bù yì yuǎn hū?”

examples.text: 曾子曰：「士不可以不弘毅，任重而道远。仁以为己任，不亦重乎？死而后已，不亦远乎？」

definitions.text: Used as a light verb to allow nouns and noun-like forms to function as active verbs. The verb itself has little to no real meaning. The noun functions as a direct object of the verb, being able to take particles such as the accusative case marker -을 or the topic marker -은.
Used as a light verb to allow nouns and noun-like forms to function as adjectives. The verb itself has little to no real meaning. The noun can be separated by the topic marker -은.
After certain roots, fully suffixed to form an inseparable verb or adjective. Such roots tend to be single-character Sino-Korean morphemes.
Used with no real meaning after a verb or adjective nominalized with -기 and followed by a particle.
Used as the neutral verbal element after suffixes expressing intent.
Used as the neutral verbal element for constructions with repeated suffixes.
